crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Self-Driving Laboratories
children.blurb: Self-driving laboratories are lab systems that close the loop between experiment design, robotic execution, measurement, and model update.

children.name: Digital Twins for Experiments
children.blurb: Digital twins for experiments are computational models of a physical experiment, instrument, or sample that stay synchronized with real data.

children.name: Instrument and Sensor Data
children.blurb: Instrument and sensor data is the stream of measurements that laboratory instruments and sensors produce, together with the context that makes those measurements meaningful.

children.name: Optimising Lab Protocols
children.blurb: Optimising lab protocols covers the design, scheduling, and revision of experimental procedures so that they use less time, reagent, and labour while producing more reliable results.

children.name: Forecasting Lab Supplies
children.blurb: Forecasting lab supplies covers the prediction of demand for reagents, consumables, and small equipment in a laboratory, from pipette tips and culture plates to antibodies and solvents.

sections.body: Laboratory automation and simulation is about using AI to run experiments, model them, and manage the surrounding logistics. In practice, self-driving labs combine robotic liquid handlers, scheduling software, and machine learning to choose next experiments, run them, and analyse results with less human intervention. Digital twins for experiments create computational replicas of instruments, samples, or whole workflows so researchers can test conditions before touching physical material. Instrument and sensor data work turns raw signals from spectrometers, microscopes, and environmental sensors into structured measurements that models can use. Optimising lab protocols uses search and Bayesian methods to tune temperatures, timings, and reagent ratios, while forecasting lab supplies uses time series and inventory models to predict demand for consumables and avoid shortages. These are not fully autonomous science, they are narrow loops where AI assists specific steps.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature, others are early, and instrument and sensor data pipelines are widely used, with many labs already relying on automated calibration and peak picking. Digital twins for experiments are common in engineering and some biology, but faithful twins for complex living systems remain hard because biological variation is large. Self-driving laboratories have shown closed-loop discovery in chemistry and materials, yet most systems still need human oversight, and the range of experiments they can run is narrow. Optimising lab protocols works well when the search space is bounded and the objective is clear, but it struggles with noisy measurements and hidden variables. Forecasting lab supplies is often solved at the level of simple demand planning, though it breaks down when supply chains are disrupted or when experiments change quickly. The honest limits are integration, data standardisation, and the cost of maintaining robots and models over time.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section fit together as a pipeline from physical execution to planning. Self-Driving Laboratories is the entry point for closed-loop systems that plan, run, and learn from experiments. Digital Twins for Experiments explains how virtual models of instruments and samples support prediction and control before physical runs, while Instrument and Sensor Data covers the raw input layer, the calibration, filtering, and feature extraction that every other page depends on. Optimising Lab Protocols focuses on the decision layer, where AI searches for better experimental conditions, and Forecasting Lab Supplies looks outward to logistics, connecting lab demand to inventory and procurement. A reader can start with Self-Driving Laboratories for the big picture, then move to Digital Twins for Experiments and Instrument and Sensor Data for the technical foundations, and finish with Optimising Lab Protocols and Forecasting Lab Supplies for the operational side. The site library holds 288 research papers, and these pages draw on that broader evidence base.
